lines.en: You send a friend a cat photo. Ding, it arrives right away.
But the photo didn't fly straight there.
The moment you hit send, step one: make it smaller.
The original is too big and slow to send, so the app quietly compresses it: smaller, yet it looks about the same.
Next, the photo reaches stop two: the server.
That's the chat app's relay station in the cloud. The photo waits here to be picked up.
Only then comes step three: the notification.
The server taps your friend's phone: "Hey, a photo for you."
That's when the phone goes ding.
After the notification, your friend's phone goes to the server and fetches the photo.
So on a slow connection, you see it blurry for a moment, then suddenly sharp.
Behind that one ding is a silent relay.
Unless you ticked "Original", what your friend gets is just a compressed copy of the cat.
The real original has been on your phone all along.
